title: NFC Social Media Tag — Tap-to-Follow Any Profile
summary: NFC social media tags carry a NTAG213 chip programmed with Instagram / LinkedIn / TikTok / YouTube / X / Linktree URL — letting your audience follow your social profiles with a single phone tap. Universal Links (iOS) + App Links (Android) auto-resolve to native social apps where installed (70-85% native app open rate), browser fallback otherwise. Multi-link landing-page option (Linktree / Beacons.ai / Stan Store / self-hosted) bundles all channels through one tap. Available as epoxy stickers, PVC business cards, table stands, key tags and wristbands for influencers, creators, restaurants, retail brands, real-estate agents and event marketers. Documented 5-15% tap-to-follow rate vs <2% QR baseline.
heroPoints: One tap to follow — phone opens your social profile directly in native app (where installed) or browser, ready to follow or connect.
Multi-link landing page option — one tag links to all your social profiles (Instagram + LinkedIn + TikTok + YouTube + Linktree).
No app required — works natively on iPhone XS+ (iOS 14+ background NDEF) and all NFC Android phones — covers 95%+ of smartphone users.

sections.title: Challenges businesses and creators face growing social followings at physical touchpoints

items.label: Printed QR scan rate in low-light environment
NFC tap-to-follow rate at restaurant table
Universal Links / App Links native app open rate

bullets: At events and retail locations, staff verbally direct customers to find and follow social profiles. Conversion rates are below 5% because typing a handle or searching on a phone takes 30-60 seconds and most people don't bother.
Printed QR codes on table cards and displays require good lighting, a steady hand, and the camera app to be open. In dim restaurant or event environments, QR scan rates drop to 1-3% of opportunities.

Businesses using multiple social platforms (Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube) need to push visitors to a single entry point, but existing multi-link pages require typing a URL rather than a single-action interaction.

Physical marketing assets (signage, packaging, merchandise) have a fixed URL that cannot be updated. If the social handle changes or a new platform is prioritised, all printed materials become outdated immediately.

For B2B use cases (real estate, professional services), exchanging LinkedIn contact details via business cards results in under 20% connection follow-through after events due to card-to-phone friction.

faq.question: Can one tag link to multiple social profiles?
faq.answer: Yes. We can encode a link to a multi-link landing page (like Linktree, Beacons.ai or your own custom page) that displays buttons for all your social channels. The user taps the NFC tag, the landing page opens, and they choose which platform to follow you on.

faq.question: Can I update the social link later without replacing the tag?
faq.answer: If the tag is encoded with a direct URL (e.g., instagram.com/brand), you would need to rewrite the tag to change it. If the tag links to a landing page you control (e.g., yourdomain.com/social), you can update the destination anytime by editing the landing page — no need to touch the physical tags.

faq.question: How many followers can I gain from NFC tags?
faq.answer: Results vary by placement and context. Restaurant table stands typically see 5-15% tap-to-follow conversion. Event wristband taps can achieve 10-25% conversion due to higher engagement context. The key advantage over QR codes is the lower friction — tapping is faster and more reliable than scanning, especially in low-light event environments.

faq.question: Do Instagram, TikTok and LinkedIn open in the native app or in the browser when the tag is tapped?
faq.answer: Both iOS and Android use app-link resolution (Universal Links on iOS, App Links on Android) to prefer the native app when it is installed. Instagram URLs (instagram.com/username) open in the Instagram app if installed, otherwise in the default browser. Same for TikTok (tiktok.com/@username), LinkedIn (linkedin.com/in/username), YouTube (youtube.com/@channel) and X / Twitter (x.com/username). Native app open rates average 70-85% across a typical audience (most users have the app of the platform they actively use). For maximum deep-link reliability we can encode the platform-specific deep-link scheme as a fallback, but the https:// universal-link form is strongly preferred because iOS Core NFC background reading silently ignores custom schemes.

faq.question: How does the Linktree / Beacons / Stan Store multi-link landing-page pattern compare to encoding a direct social URL?
faq.answer: Trade-off on discoverability vs funnel control. Encoding a direct URL (instagram.com/brand) converts faster because it takes the user to the follow button in one tap — ideal for campaigns pushing a specific channel. The multi-link page pattern (Linktree, Beacons.ai, Stan Store, Bio Link, Koji, or a self-hosted page on your domain) adds one extra click but gives you a funnel you can re-sort, add or remove channels from without touching the physical tag. Creators with a dominant channel prefer direct encoding; multi-channel businesses (restaurants pushing Instagram + Google reviews + reservation link) prefer multi-link. Multi-link pages also give you first-party analytics (Linktree Pro, Beacons Plus or your own GA4) showing which channels actually convert per placement, which is strategically valuable for cross-channel attribution. We typically recommend encoding a redirect URL on your own domain so you can pivot between direct-URL and multi-link-page destinations without replacing any tags.
